t: Hereditary succession had no precedent in Islamic history, and Yazid's nomination by Mu'awiya was refused by Husayn and by the sons of other prominent companions of Muhammad.
Husayn's companions numbered thirty-two horsemen and forty infantrymen in most accounts, against an army of 4,000 that Shia sources say grew to 30,000.
The battle is central to Shia history and tradition, remembered every year in Muharram and on Ashura, and modern historians still disagree about what Husayn intended.
dyk: Theophilus of Edessa's history, preserved in later Christian chronicles, corroborates the death of Husayn and most of his men at Karbala after suffering from thirst, but appears to say that he was killed by Mu'awiya as the final engagement of the First Fitna.
ev: Ali is assassinated, and his son Hasan signs a treaty handing power to Mu'awiya
Mu'awiya nominates his son Yazid as his successor
Mu'awiya dies, and Yazid demands allegiance from Husayn and other dissidents
Husayn leaves Mecca for Kufa with about fifty men and his family
Husayn is stopped by Kufan troops and camps at Karbala, where a second army arrives
The Kufan army attacks on 10 Muharram, and Husayn is killed with most of his companions
The Tawwabin, who rose in remorse for Husayn's death, are mostly killed at Ayn al-Warda
Mukhtar al-Thaqafi's forces rout an Umayyad army at Khazir, and Ibn Ziyad is slain

f.place: Karbala, a desert plain about 70 kilometres north of Kufa, in modern-day southern Iraq
f.sides: The forces of the Umayyad caliph Yazid I, under Umar ibn Sa'd with the governor Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad directing, an army of 4,000, which Shia sources say grew to 30,000; and a small party led by Husayn ibn Ali, whose companions numbered thirty-two horsemen and forty infantrymen in most accounts, and a few hundred in some
f.outcome: Husayn was killed with most of his family and close companions, and the surviving members of his family were taken captive to Kufa and then to Damascus.
